source_text:
Ἰσαὰκ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον
συνεποδίζετο καὶ ἀμνὸς ἀντ' αὐτοῦ ἐσφάζετο, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ σταυροῦ ἀνεφέρετο καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐσταυροῦτο καὶ πάσχουσα ἡ σὰρξ ἡ θεότης οὐκ ἔπασχεν. Ἔστη τὸ ἱστίον τοῦ σταυροῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἀναυάγητος ἔμεινεν· τούτῳ τῷ ἱστίῳ τοῦ σταυροῦ ὁ πλέων ναυάγιον θανάτου οὐκ οἶδεν, ἀλλὰ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναπλέει. Οὐκέτι Εὔα φοβεῖται τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Ἀδάμ, ἐν γὰρ Μαρίᾳ τὸ ταύτης πταῖσμα ἀνασέσωσται· οὐκέτι Ἀδὰμ φοβεῖται τὸν ὄφιν, Χριστὸς γὰρ συνέτριψεν τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δράκοντος· Σὺ γάρ, φησίν, συνέτριψας τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δράκοντος ἐπὶ τοῦ ὕδατος, τουτέστιν ἐπὶ τοῦ βαπτίσματος. Οὐκέτι πενθῶ, οὐκέτι κλαίω λέγων· Ἐστράφην εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν ἐν τῷ ἐμπαγῆναί μοι ἄκανθαν· ἐλθὼν γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς τὴν ἄκανθαν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἐκριζώσας τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κεφαλῇ ἐπέθηκεν. Λέλυταί μου ἡ ἀρχαία λύπη, λέλυται ἡ παλαιὰ ἀρὰ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀνατελεῖ σοι ἡ γῆ· ἐξηράνθησαν γὰρ αἱ ἄκανθαι, ἐξεριζώθη ὁ τρίβολος καὶ τρίπλοκος στέφανος τῇ κεφαλῇ μου ἐπετέθη. Τίς Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἑλλήνων πιστεύει ὅτι ξύλον ἔστη καὶ ζωὴν ἐξήνθησεν; καὶ καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ὑπὸ πιστῶν τρυγᾶται καὶ ὁ καρπὸς ἀδαπάνητος μένει· καὶ πᾶσα φυλὴ καὶ πᾶν ἔθνος πιστῶν ἐπὶ τοῦτο τὸ δένδρον βήματι ψυχῆς ἀναβαίνει καὶ τὸν κόλπον τῆς διανοίας ἀθανάτου καρποῦ πληροῖ, καὶ πάντας βαστάζει τὸ δένδρον καὶ πάντας χορτάζει καὶ σφραγίζει καὶ πλουτίζει καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀκοντίζει. Τί γὰρ δι' ἡμᾶς οὐχ ὑπέμεινεν κληθῆναι Χριστός; Οὐ δυνάμεθα ἐξαριθμήσασθαι αὐτοῦ τὰ ὀνόματα, ἐπιχείρω δὲ λέγειν, ἀγαπητοί· θύρα, ὁδός, πρόβατον, ποιμήν, σκώληξ, λίθος, μαργαρίτης, ἄνθος, ἄγγελος, ἄνθρωπος, θεός, φῶς, πηγή, ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης. Ὁ πολυώνυμος Χριστὸς καὶ εἷς ὑπάρχων, πολυώνυμος ὁ υἱὸς καὶ εἷς ὢν οὐ τρεπόμενος, οὐ μεταβαλλόμενος, ἄτρεπτος γὰρ ἡ θεότης· ἀλλ' ἑκάστῳ πράγματι κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν ἁρμοζόμενος ἴδιον ὄνομα ἑκάστῃ ἐνεργείᾳ τεθεικώς. Καὶ ἴδωμεν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰ δυνάμεθα ἑκάστῳ ὀνόματι τὴν ἐνέργειαν παραστῆσαι. Ὁδὸς ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι, φησίν, ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἀρχηγὸς πασῶν τῶν ἀρετῶν καὶ τῆς εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναβάσεως γέγονεν. Ὁ αὐτὸς θύρα· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ἡ θύρα τῶν προβάτων, ἐπειδὴ δι' αὐτοῦ καθάπερ διὰ θύρας εἰς τὴν τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείαν εἰσερχόμεθα. Ἅλας ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ τὴν δυσωδίαν τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπέσμηξεν καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν πρὸς νοστὸν εὐσεβείας τῇ πίστει ἤρτυσεν καὶ τὰ λελυμένα μέλη τῆς διανοίας τῇ ἀληθείᾳ συνέσφιγξεν.
thought_title: The many names of Christ and their works
orientation: Amphilochius continues his homily on the newly baptized, now moving from the cross as bridal chamber to the many names of Christ and what each name reveals about his saving work.
pass_a_gloss: Isaac upon the altar was bound together [by the feet] and a lamb in place of him was slaughtered, and the Son of God upon a cross was carried up and in the flesh on behalf of us was crucified and suffering the flesh the divinity not was suffering. Stood the mast of the cross in the ship of the world and the world unshipwrecked remained; with this mast of the cross the [one] sailing shipwreck of death not knows, but into heavens sails up. No longer Eve fears the reproach of Adam, for in Mary the of this one [Eve's] fall has been saved; no longer Adam fears the serpent, for Christ crushed the head of the dragon; You for, he says, crushed the head of the dragon upon the water, that is upon the baptism. No longer I mourn, no longer I weep saying: I was turned into misery in the being stuck in me [a] thorn; for having come Christ the thorn of the sins of us having uprooted upon his own head placed [it]. Has been loosed of me the ancient grief, has been loosed the old curse the [one] saying: Thorns and thistles will sprout up to you the earth; for were dried up the thorns, was uprooted the thistle and [a] threefold crown upon the head of me was placed. Who of Jews and Greeks believes that wood stood and life blossomed? and each day by faithful [ones] is harvested and the fruit unconsumed remains; and every tribe and every nation of faithful [ones] upon this the tree with step of soul goes up and the bosom of the mind with immortal fruit fills, and all bears the tree and all feeds and seals and enriches and after these things into heavens hurls. What for on behalf of us not did he endure to be called Christ? Not we are able to enumerate of him the names, I attempt but to say, beloved [ones]; door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness. The many-named Christ and one being, many-named the Son and one being not turning, not changing, for unchangeable the divinity; but to each matter according to the activity fitting [himself] [a] proper name to each activity having set. And let us see, beloved [ones], if we are able to each name the activity to present. Way he was called: I for am, he says, the way and the truth, since he [the] leader of all the virtues and of the into heavens ascent has become. The same [one] door: I for am the door of the sheep, since through him just as through [a] door into the of the heavens kingdom we enter. Salt he was called, since the stench of the idolatry of men he wiped away and the souls of us to [a] relish of piety with the faith seasoned and the loosened members of the mind with the truth bound together.

lemmas.gloss: was being bound hand and foot

choices.english: a ram was being slain in his place
choices.why: ἀμνός is the adult male sheep, the ram caught in the thicket in Gen 22:13, not a lamb; the substitutionary sense of ἀντ' αὐτοῦ must be kept
rejected: a lamb was being slain in his place
a sheep was being slaughtered instead of him

choices.why: ἱστίον means sail, not mast; the cross is the sail that drives the world's ship safely
ἀνασῴζω has a medical/soteriological sense of being saved, healed, or restored; 'made good' loses the healing nuance
rejected: her fault has been made good

choices.term: τὴν ἄκανθαν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἐκριζώσας τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κεφαλῇ ἐπέθηκεν
choices.english: having uprooted the thorn of our sins, he placed it on his own head
choices.why: ἐκριζώσας is the aorist participle of uprooting; the action of rooting out the thorn must be explicit, and the thorn (crown of thorns) is what is placed on Christ's head
rejected: he placed the thorn of our sins on his own head
having removed the thorn of our sins, he put it on his head

choices.why: The term is repeated emphatically; 'many-named' preserves the compound structure and the rhetorical repetition
ἀποσμήχω means to wipe off or cleanse away; the stench of idolatry is removed by Christ as salt

pass_b_english: Isaac was being hobbled at the altar, and a lamb was being slain in his place; and the Son of God was being lifted up on the cross, and in the flesh he was being crucified for us, and though the flesh suffered, the divinity did not suffer. The sail of the cross stood in the ship of the world, and the world remained unshipwrecked; the one who sails with this sail of the cross knows no shipwreck of death, but sails up into the heavens. Eve no longer fears the reproach of Adam, for in Mary her fault has been healed; Adam no longer fears the serpent, for Christ has crushed the head of the dragon. For you, he says, crushed the head of the dragon upon the water (Psalm 74:13–14, LXX 73:13–14, alluding to baptism), that is, upon baptism. I no longer mourn, I no longer weep saying, I was turned to hardship when a thorn was planted in me; for Christ came, and having uprooted the thorn of our sins, he placed it on his own head. My ancient grief is released, the old curse is released that says, Thorns and thistles the earth shall bring forth for you (Genesis 3:18); for the thorns are dried up, the thistle is uprooted, and a triple-woven crown is placed on my head. Who among Jews and Greeks believes that wood stood and life blossomed? And every day it is harvested by the faithful, and the fruit remains unspent; and every tribe and every nation of the faithful climbs this tree with the step of the soul and fills the bosom of the mind with immortal fruit, and the tree carries all and feeds all and seals all and enriches all, and after these things hurls them into the heavens. For what name did Christ not endure to be called for our sake? We cannot count his names, but I attempt to speak, beloved: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness. The many-named Christ is also one; many-named is the Son, and being one he is not turned, not changed, for the divinity is unchanging; but fitting himself to each matter according to the working, he has set a proper name for each working. And let us see, beloved, if we can present the working for each name. He was called way: For I am, he says, the way and the truth (John 14:6), since he himself has become the leader of all the virtues and of the ascent into the heavens. The same one is door: For I am the door of the sheep (John 10:7), since through him as through a door we enter into the kingdom of the heavens. He was called salt, since he wiped away the stench of the idolatry of human beings and seasoned our souls for the savor of piety by faith, and bound together the loosened limbs of the mind by the truth.

problems.quote: a ram was being slain in his place
problems.why: ἀμνὸς means 'lamb', not 'ram'; this is the typological lamb
problems.fix: a lamb was being slain in his place

problems.quote: a threefold crown is placed on my head
problems.source_quote: τρίπλοκος στέφανος τῇ κεφαλῇ μου ἐπετέθη
problems.why: τρίπλοκος means 'woven of three strands' or 'triple-twined', not 'threefold crown' which suggests three crowns
problems.fix: a triple-woven crown is placed on my head

problems.quote: Isaac was being bound hand and foot on the altar
problems.why: συνεποδίζετο means 'was being hobbled/fettered at the feet', not 'bound hand and foot'
problems.fix: Isaac was being hobbled at the altar
problems.ruling: συνεποδίζετο from συνεποδίζω means bound at feet specifically; 'hand and foot' adds unsupported detail.

problems.quote: For what did Christ not endure to be called for our sake?
problems.source_quote: Τί γὰρ δι' ἡμᾶς οὐχ ὑπέμεινεν κληθῆναι Χριστός;
problems.why: The rhetorical question means 'What name did Christ not endure to be called for our sake?', not 'what did he endure'
problems.fix: For what name did Christ not endure to be called for our sake?
problems.ruling: Context is listing names Christ endured being called; 'what did he endure' loses the 'what name' sense of τί.

problems.why: Ἅλας is missing from the list of names in the English text; it was listed in the source names but omitted in translation
problems.ruling: Ἅλας ἤκουσεν means 'he was called salt'; English omits ἅλας from the name list, breaking the enumeration.

edits.old: a ram was being slain in his place
edits.new: a lamb was being slain in his place

edits.old: a threefold crown is placed on my head
edits.new: a triple-woven crown is placed on my head

edits.old: Isaac was being bound hand and foot on the altar
edits.new: Isaac was being hobbled at the altar

edits.old: For what did Christ not endure to be called for our sake?
edits.new: For what name did Christ not endure to be called for our sake?

fixed: ἀμνὸς means 'lamb', not 'ram'; corrected to 'a lamb was being slain in his place'.
τρίπλοκος means 'woven of three strands' or 'triple-twined', not 'threefold'; corrected to 'a triple-woven crown is placed on my head'.
συνεποδίζετο means 'was being hobbled/fettered at the feet', not 'bound hand and foot'; corrected to 'Isaac was being hobbled at the altar'.
The rhetorical question asks what name Christ endured to be called; corrected to 'For what name did Christ not endure to be called for our sake?'.
The problem about 'He was called salt' is not a mistranslation; the English already contains 'He was called salt' in the final sentence, so no edit is needed.

problems.quote: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness.
problems.source_quote: θύρα, ὁδός, πρόβατον, ποιμήν, σκώληξ, λίθος, μαργαρίτης, ἄνθος, ἄγγελος, ἄνθρωπος, θεός, φῶς, πηγή, ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης
problems.why: The list omits ἅλας (salt), which appears in the source between the names list and the salt exposition below.
problems.fix: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness, salt.
problems.ruling: ἅλας (salt) is in the source list at line 14 but omitted from English list at line 7.

problems.why: Ἅλας is missing from the list of names in the English text earlier; it appears here without prior mention, breaking the pattern of 'He was called X.'
problems.fix: Add 'salt' to the list: 'door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness, salt'
problems.ruling: Ἅλας ἤκουσεν = 'He heard salt'; 'He was called salt' implies prior listing, but ἅλας is absent from the names list above.

edits.old: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness.
edits.new: door, way, sheep, shepherd, worm, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, spring, sun of righteousness, salt.

fixed: Added 'salt' to the list of names, since the source includes ἅλας in the list (θύρα, ὁδός, πρόβατον, ποιμήν, σκώληξ, λίθος, μαργαρίτης, ἄνθος, ἄγγελος, ἄνθρωπος, θεός, φῶς, πηγή, ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης, ἅλας). The second problem is the same omission and is fixed by this edit.

problems.source_quote: ἐπὶ τοῦ ὕδατος, τουτέστιν ἐπὶ τοῦ βαπτίσματος
problems.why: The citation given is wrong: Ps 74:13 LXX speaks of crushing Leviathan's heads in the sea, but the homilist quotes 'upon the water' as baptism, not the exact verse.

problems.quote: I was turned to misery when a thorn was stuck in me
problems.source_quote: Ἐστράφην εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν ἐν τῷ ἐμπαγῆναί μοι ἄκανθαν
problems.why: Missing the allusion to Genesis 3:18; 'talaiperia' echoes the curse, and 'en to empagēnai' is 'when a thorn was fixed/planted in me' — the thorn is the curse itself.
problems.fix: I was turned to hardship when a thorn was planted in me

problems.quote: and the flesh suffered but the divinity did not suffer
problems.source_quote: καὶ πάσχουσα ἡ σὰρξ ἡ θεότης οὐκ ἔπασχεν
problems.why: Source says 'the divinity did not suffer' without stating the flesh suffered; English adds 'the flesh suffered' as a clause.
problems.fix: and though the flesh suffered, the divinity did not suffer
problems.ruling: πάσχουσα is a participial modifier 'suffering' modifying σάρξ, not a main clause; English adds 'the flesh suffered' as independent clause, changing syntax and emphasis.

edits.old: I was turned to misery when a thorn was stuck in me
edits.new: I was turned to hardship when a thorn was planted in me

edits.old: and the flesh suffered but the divinity did not suffer
edits.new: and though the flesh suffered, the divinity did not suffer

fixed: Wrong scripture citation: the source alludes to Ps 74:13–14 LXX (73:13–14) and applies it to baptism, so the citation is corrected.
Mistranslation: 'ταλαιπωρίαν' is better rendered 'hardship' to echo the curse of Genesis 3:18, and 'ἐμπαγῆναί' means 'planted' rather than 'stuck'.
Omission: the source says 'suffering the flesh, the divinity did not suffer'; the English added a separate clause 'the flesh suffered', so it is corrected to 'though the flesh suffered'.

fixed.note: The Greek list of names ends with ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης; "salt" was added to the list and only comes up later in the passage.

dismissed.quote: seasoned our souls for the savor of piety by faith
dismissed.why: 'For the savor' is awkward and misleading; πρὸς νοστὸν εὐσεβείας means 'toward the return/homecoming of piety' or 'for the sake of returning to piety.' Νοστός means 'return home,' not 'savor' (which would be νοστιμ-). This is a serious error confusing νοστός with νόστιμος.
dismissed.note: The image is salt seasoning the soul (ἤρτυσεν), so νοστόν here means taste or savor, not "return"; "savor" fits.
